entries.title: II Kings 11:1
segments:
Destroyed all the seed royal; so that she might reign without a rival. 
 
Love of power tends to destroy natural affection, and leads not only to the violation of the rights of humanity, but to the commission of the most abominable crimes.

entries.title: II Kings 11:4
segments:
Jehoiada; the high-priest. 
 
  Fetched the rulers over hundreds; he had previously assembled the Levites and chiefs of the fathers of Israel out of all parts of the kingdom, that he might have a force sufficient to withstand Athaliah.

Subjects are not always bound to obey their rulers, but may be called in extraordinary cases to set them aside, and place others in their stead; and if need be, to bring about a revolution for this purpose.

entries.title: II Kings 11:5
segments: Enter in on the Sabbath; take your weekly turn in ministering at the temple.

entries.title: II Kings 11:7
segments: Go forth on the Sabbath; are released after your week's service at the temple.

entries.title: II Kings 11:8
segments:
Ye shall compass the king; to prevent his being slain by the partisans of Athaliah. 
 
  Within the ranges; the lines of guards.

entries.title: II Kings 11:12
segments: The testimony; a copy of the law of Moses. Compare
No king can be safe on his throne, or magistrate preserve his authority, without the providential care and gracious aid of God.

entries.title: II Kings 11:14
segments: That treatment which, without remorse, persons have unjustly shown towards others who were innocent, they are ready to stigmatize as enormous wickedness when justly shown towards themselves.

entries.title: II Kings 11:20
segments: When rulers receive their authority as from God, and use it according to his will, quietness, peace, and prosperity may be expected throughout the land.
